minutes.headline: Conservation Commission continued the Goodridge Street driveway hearing to Jan 22 and approved a stormwater system and a Pine Grove Road renovation.
minutes.summary: The Commission heard several wetlands hearings and continued three (157 Goodridge Street driveway, 400 Lunenburg-Shirley Road amendment, 390 Howard Street) to January 22. It approved the DNA Lunenburg stormwater NOI and the 50 Pine Grove Road NOI, acted on certificates of compliance, and discussed violations, FY26 budget requests, wildlands, and farmland of local importance.

public_comment.topic: North County Land Trust director described a planned March landowner conservation workshop for Lunenburg and neighboring towns and asked for a town liaison and help identifying landowners.
public_comment.stated_role: director of conservation and climate, North County Land Trust

public_comment.topic: A resident (Lynn) commented on wildlands designation by deed and the possibility of designating the Town Forest.

budget_items.topic: FY26 continuing education budget for commissioners
budget_items.what_was_said: The agent needs budget requests to accounting by the 20th. The commission discussed class counts and per-class costs.
The commission agreed to budget handbook access for all members and staff at a nominal subscription cost.

budget_items.topic: Flyer with tax mailings and Ledger ad
budget_items.what_was_said: The chair recommended budgeting yearly for a flyer with tax mailings and a quarter-page Ledger ad, citing last year's estimate.

budget_items.topic: North County Land Trust workshop co-sponsorship
budget_items.what_was_said: The land trust mentioned that a small contribution from the commission would be welcome but not expected.
A member said the grant might cover part of an acquisition cost, but could not recall the share.

budget_items.topic: Snow Riders recreational trails grant closeout
budget_items.what_was_said: The 2022 grant was closed out, with volunteer time and equipment-use equivalents cited as community benefit.
A fine was paid to the treasurer by the property owner.
A member noted that conservation land management money comes only from the timber harvesting fund.

decisions.decision: Hearing on 157 Goodridge Street to be continued so an abutter without a computer can attend in person; applicant to consider driveway pitch, drainage and demarcation of the 30-foot zone.
Magnesium chloride was noted as a lower-impact deicer if one is needed; no deicing condition was imposed.
The agent will carry the budget asks (class counts, handbooks, tax-mailing flyer, Ledger ad) into the FY26 request; no formal vote was taken.
The agent will notify the town manager and select board about personal property placed on town land at 40 Fire Road; the certificate of compliance is held until the violation is cleared.
A special meeting is set for January 29 to hear the lake community reports; the next regular meeting is January 22.
A member will look into local paint-drop-off options before the commission decides on a paint stewardship program.
The agent will recirculate the land trust flyer, and the chair will contact the open space committee chair about the workshop.

what_happened.line: The Commission continued the 157 Goodridge Street driveway hearing to January 22 so an abutter without a computer could attend in person.
The Commission approved the DNA Lunenburg stormwater notice of intent on the September plans, with no buffer-zone changes; one member abstained.
The Commission approved the 50 Pine Grove Road notice of intent, 4-0 with one abstention.
The Commission continued the 400 Lunenburg-Shirley Road amendment and the 390 Howard Street hearing to January 22.
The Commission approved two certificates of compliance, denied a third for 32 Pine Grove Road until stabilized, and voted to send a letter to the 10 Mass Ave owner.

why_it_matters: Three wetlands hearings stay open until January 22, so abutters on Goodridge Street, Lunenburg-Shirley Road and Howard Street still have a chance to be heard before a decision.

The commission's FY26 budget asks (continuing education, handbooks, a tax-mailing flyer, a Ledger ad) were set as direction to the agent with no vote, so they will reach the town budget as requests, not decisions.
watch_next: January 22: the next regular meeting, with the three continued hearings.
January 29: a special meeting to hear the lake community reports.

reconciliation.what: Our minutes against the minutes the town published. caption_error = the same fact the captions rendered badly, resolved by the official reading shown beside the as-heard one; discrepancy = a substantive difference, flagged and not resolved. Neither record is treated as the referee.
reconciliation.summary: The two records agree on every motion and its outcome, but every vote tally differs by one: ours shows 5-0 or 4-0-1 and the official 6-0 or 5-0-1. The likely cause is the chair's vote missing from our count, so check the recording. The official also leaves out several figures and follow-ups we recorded, and one grant figure ($116,000 vs $16,000) differs.
